1	"""KMS/HSM provider abstraction.
2	
3	Every private key is owned by a *provider*: a local software key store by
4	default, or an external KMS/HSM reached through the ``module:factory`` entry
5	point named by ``KEYMGR_PROVIDER``. The rest of the package never touches raw
6	key material when a provider is in use: it only persists the opaque
7	``provider_id`` / ``handle`` / ``encrypted_material`` triple a provider
8	returns, and asks the provider to turn a handle back into exportable material.
9	
10	Primary/standby failover
11	------------------------
12	``KEYMGR_PROVIDER_CHAIN`` may name a comma-separated list of ``local`` /
13	``module:factory`` entries (entries and their built ``provider_id`` values
14	must be unique; an unset variable falls back to ``KEYMGR_PROVIDER``, while a
15	set-but-empty, empty-item or malformed chain is unusable). The first healthy
16	entry is activated. Every ORDINARY provider call then shares ONE
17	non-resettable five-second budget started at its first wait or probe: every
18	gate wait and every health probe of the attempt draws on the same deadline,
19	and a single ``health()`` probe is additionally capped at one second. A probe
20	returning exactly ``True`` clears the persisted failure count and proceeds;
21	``False``, a non-bool, a raised probe, one past its wait, or a result that
22	arrives only after the wait (void -- it never counts as anything but the
23	timeout) increments the active entry's persisted failure count (capped at
24	three) and pins the call to the fixed 503. The first two failures never
25	switch; after the third failure the call uses the REMAINDER of the same
26	five-second budget to re-verify the active entry (still at most one second
27	per probe) -- recovery clears the count and serves the call -- and otherwise
28	probes the standby entries in chain order under the same cross-process
29	intent/drain gate a reconnect uses, failing over exactly once to the first
30	healthy standby (a single ``switching`` then ``ready`` commit, generation
31	plus one) and continuing in the new generation. Old calls finish on the
32	instance they captured, later calls land on the new generation, and
33	concurrent third strikes build/commit exactly once. With no healthy standby
34	(or on a gate timeout) the old generation is retained. The threshold lives in
35	``provider-health.json`` (a 0600 satellite of a READY ``provider-state.json``
36	with the same id and generation), so it survives restarts and is shared
37	across processes; a corrupt, ahead or same-generation-wrong-id health record
38	is a fixed 503 that is never rewritten. A recovered primary is never
39	re-selected automatically; only ``reconnect`` re-selects the first healthy
40	entry, while ``switchover`` moves the active provider to one NAMED chain
41	entry under the same gate (``switching`` then ``ready`` commits, reason
42	``reconnect``). Pending idempotent operations stay bound to their original
43	``provider_id`` and are never replayed on a standby.
44	
45	Provider contract
46	-----------------
47	A provider instance exposes:
48	
49	* ``provider_id``: a non-empty string;
50	* ``capabilities``: ``{"algorithms": ["AES256", "RSA2048"],
51	  "operations": ["generate", "rotate", "import_material",
52	  "export_material", "delete"]}``;
53	* ``generate(algorithm)`` / ``rotate(algorithm)`` ->
54	  ``{"handle", "public_key", "encrypted_material"}``;
55	* ``import_material(algorithm, public_key, material)`` -> the same triple;
56	* ``export_material(handle)`` -> ``{"public_key", "encrypted_material"}``;
57	* ``delete(handle)`` -> ``None``, idempotent;
58	* ``health()`` -> ``bool``, *optional*. A missing method is treated as ready;
59	  a method that raises or returns anything but a real bool reports unavailable.
60	  The probe's own text never leaves the process.
61	
62	Native signing (optional)
63	-------------------------
64	``capabilities["operations"]`` MAY additionally list ``"sign"``. Declaring it
65	makes ``sign(handle: str, message: bytes) -> bytes`` contractual: a provider
66	that declares the operation without a callable ``sign`` method fails the
67	contract (and a declared-but-non-callable ``sign`` attribute is invalid too).
68	The method signs with RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5/SHA-256 inside the KMS/HSM and returns
69	the 256-byte signature; private material never crosses the boundary. A handle
70	that is not a non-empty string raises ``ValueError``, a non-bytes message
71	raises ``TypeError``, and an unknown handle, a handle that is not an RSA key,
72	or any backend failure raises :class:`ProviderUnavailable`. When a version's
73	owning provider declares ``sign``, the service calls it on the bound provider
74	inside the ordinary five-second provider-call gate, never calls
75	``export_material`` for signing and never loads the private key into the
76	service process; it verifies the returned signature against the version's
77	stored public key and treats a malformed result, a failed verification or any
78	provider exception as the fixed 503 (no audit event). A provider that does
79	NOT declare ``sign`` keeps the export-based signing path. The built-in local
80	provider declares and implements ``sign``.
81	
82	Native DEK unwrap (optional)
83	----------------------------
84	``capabilities["operations"]`` MAY additionally list ``"unwrap_key"``.
85	Declaring it makes
86	``unwrap_key(handle: str, wrapped_key: bytes, wrap_nonce: bytes | None = None) -> bytes``
87	contractual: a provider that declares the operation without a callable
88	``unwrap_key`` method fails the contract (and a declared-but-non-callable
89	``unwrap_key`` attribute is invalid too). The method unwraps a
90	``keymgr-envelope-v1`` data key inside the KMS/HSM and returns the 32-byte
91	DEK; the KEK's private material never crosses the boundary. A handle that is
92	not a non-empty string raises ``ValueError``; a non-bytes ``wrapped_key`` or
93	a non-null non-bytes ``wrap_nonce`` raises ``TypeError``; an empty
94	``wrapped_key``, an AES256 ``wrap_nonce`` that is not exactly 12 bytes or an
95	RSA2048 ``wrap_nonce`` that is not null raises ``ValueError``; an unknown
96	handle, a handle whose algorithm does not fit the request, or any backend
97	failure raises :class:`ProviderUnavailable`; an authentication failure (a
98	tampered or wrong-key ``wrapped_key``) raises
99	:class:`ProviderInvalidMaterial`. When a version's owning provider declares
100	``unwrap_key``, the service's decrypt path calls it on the bound provider
101	inside the ordinary five-second provider-call gate, never calls
102	``export_material`` and never loads the KEK private key into the service
103	process; an authentication failure surfaces as a 400 naming the envelope,
104	while a malformed result or any provider fault is the fixed 503 (no audit
105	event). A provider that does NOT declare ``unwrap_key`` keeps the
106	export-based decrypt path. The built-in local provider declares and
107	implements ``unwrap_key``.
108	
109	The factory named by ``KEYMGR_PROVIDER=module:factory`` is imported lazily on
110	first use and called with no arguments. A missing module/factory, a factory
111	raising, or a returned object failing the contract all raise
112	:class:`ProviderUnavailable`; the service answers ``503`` (CLI exit ``1``) and
113	never falls back to the local provider.

342	def _validate_external(obj) -> None:
343	    """Check a factory-built object satisfies the provider contract."""
344	    provider_id = getattr(obj, "provider_id", None)
345	    if not isinstance(provider_id, str) or not provider_id:
346	        raise ProviderUnavailable(
347	            "provider factory returned an object without a non-empty provider_id"
348	        )
349	    caps = getattr(obj, "capabilities", None)
350	    if not isinstance(caps, dict):
351	        raise ProviderUnavailable(
352	            "provider %r has no capabilities mapping" % provider_id
353	        )
354	    algorithms = caps.get("algorithms")
355	    operations = caps.get("operations")
356	    if not isinstance(algorithms, (list, tuple)) or not isinstance(
357	        operations, (list, tuple)
358	    ):
359	        raise ProviderUnavailable(
360	            "provider %r capabilities must list algorithms and operations"
361	            % provider_id
362	        )
363	    missing = [a for a in SUPPORTED_ALGORITHMS if a not in algorithms]
364	    if missing:
365	        raise ProviderUnavailable(
366	            "provider %r lacks required algorithms: %s"
367	            % (provider_id, ", ".join(missing))
368	        )
369	    missing_ops = [op for op in OPERATIONS if op not in operations]
370	    if missing_ops:
371	        raise ProviderUnavailable(
372	            "provider %r lacks required operations: %s"
373	            % (provider_id, ", ".join(missing_ops))
374	        )
375	    for name in OPERATIONS:
376	        if not callable(getattr(obj, name, None)):
377	            raise ProviderUnavailable(
378	                "provider %r is missing a callable %s() operation"
379	                % (provider_id, name)
380	            )
381	    # ``sign`` is optional, but declaring it makes the method contractual: a
382	    # provider listing it without a callable sign() is invalid.
383	    if OP_SIGN in operations and not callable(getattr(obj, "sign", None)):
384	        raise ProviderUnavailable(
385	            "provider %r declares the sign operation without a callable "
386	            "sign() method" % provider_id
387	        )
388	    # ``unwrap_key`` is optional under the same rule: declaring it makes a
389	    # callable unwrap_key() method contractual.
390	    if OP_UNWRAP_KEY in operations and not callable(
391	        getattr(obj, "unwrap_key", None)
392	    ):
393	        raise ProviderUnavailable(
394	            "provider %r declares the unwrap_key operation without a "
395	            "callable unwrap_key() method" % provider_id
396	        )
397	    configure = getattr(obj, "configure", None)
398	    if configure is not None and not callable(configure):
399	        raise ProviderUnavailable(
400	            "provider %r has a non-callable configure attribute" % provider_id
401	        )
402	    # health() is optional: no attribute means always healthy. A present but
403	    # non-callable health is a contract failure like any other method.
404	    health = getattr(obj, "health", None)
405	    if health is not None and not callable(health):
406	        raise ProviderUnavailable(
407	            "provider %r has a non-callable health attribute" % provider_id
408	        )

411	class _SafeProvider:
412	    """Adapter around an external provider enforcing the error contract.
413	
414	    ProviderError subtypes pass through unchanged; any other exception the
415	    external module raises is normalized to ProviderUnavailable so a backend
416	    fault always surfaces as 503 and never as a 500 or a fallback.
417	    """
418	
419	    def __init__(self, inner) -> None:
420	        self._inner = inner
421	        self.provider_id = inner.provider_id
422	        self.capabilities = inner.capabilities
423	
424	    def configure(self, data_dir: str) -> None:
425	        try:
426	            configure = getattr(self._inner, "configure", None)
427	            if configure is not None:
428	                configure(data_dir)
429	        except ProviderError:
430	            raise
431	        except Exception as exc:
432	            raise ProviderUnavailable(
433	                "provider %r failed to initialize" % self.provider_id
434	            ) from exc
435	
436	    def _call(self, name: str, *args):
437	        method = getattr(self._inner, name)
438	        try:
439	            return method(*args)
440	        except ProviderError:
441	            raise
442	        except Exception as exc:
443	            raise ProviderUnavailable(
444	                "provider %r operation %s failed" % (self.provider_id, name)
445	            ) from exc

447	    def generate(self, algorithm: str) -> MaterialTriple:
448	        return _require_triple(self._call("generate", algorithm), "generate")
449	
450	    def rotate(self, algorithm: str) -> MaterialTriple:
451	        return _require_triple(self._call("rotate", algorithm), "rotate")
452	
453	    def import_material(self, algorithm, public_key, material) -> MaterialTriple:
454	        return _require_triple(

461	        if not isinstance(result, dict):

464	            )

467	            raise ProviderUnavailable(

480	        # Idempotent by contract; even so, a backend fault on delete is a 503

484	    def sign(self, handle: str, message: bytes) -> bytes:
485	        """KMS/HSM-native sign, with the error contract enforced.
486	
487	        Only invoked when the provider declared ``sign`` (contract validation
488	        guarantees a callable method then); a backend fault is normalized to
489	        :class:`ProviderUnavailable` like every other operation, and a result
490	        that is not bytes is a contract failure, never passed on.
491	        """
492	        if not callable(getattr(self._inner, "sign", None)):
493	            raise ProviderUnavailable(
494	                "provider %r declares sign without a callable sign() method"
495	                % self.provider_id
496	            )
497	        result = self._call("sign", handle, message)
498	        if not isinstance(result, bytes):
499	            raise ProviderUnavailable(
500	                "provider returned a non-bytes signature from sign"
501	            )
502	        return result
503	
504	    def unwrap_key(self, handle: str, wrapped_key: bytes, wrap_nonce=None) -> bytes:
505	        """KMS/HSM-native DEK unwrap, with the error contract enforced.
506	
507	        Only invoked when the provider declared ``unwrap_key`` (contract
508	        validation guarantees a callable method then). The boundary argument
509	        rules are enforced here too, so a provider cannot silently accept a
510	        malformed call: a bad handle is a ``ValueError`` and a non-bytes
511	        ``wrapped_key``/non-null non-bytes ``wrap_nonce`` a ``TypeError``,
512	        exactly as the contract requires of the method itself. The
513	        algorithm-specific nonce rules stay with the provider (only it knows
514	        the handle's algorithm). ``ValueError``/``TypeError``/
515	        :class:`ProviderError` from the provider pass through unchanged (an
516	        authentication failure surfaces as :class:`ProviderInvalidMaterial`);
517	        any other exception is a backend fault normalized to
518	        :class:`ProviderUnavailable`, and a result that is not exactly the
519	        32-byte data key is a contract failure, never passed on.
520	        """
521	        if not isinstance(handle, str) or not handle:
522	            raise ValueError("unwrap_key requires a non-empty handle string")
523	        if not isinstance(wrapped_key, bytes):
524	            raise TypeError("unwrap_key wrapped_key must be bytes")
525	        if wrap_nonce is not None and not isinstance(wrap_nonce, bytes):
526	            raise TypeError("unwrap_key wrap_nonce must be bytes or None")
527	        if not wrapped_key:
528	            raise ValueError("unwrap_key wrapped_key must be non-empty")
529	        if not callable(getattr(self._inner, "unwrap_key", None)):
530	            raise ProviderUnavailable(
531	                "provider %r declares unwrap_key without a callable "
532	                "unwrap_key() method" % self.provider_id
533	            )
534	        try:
535	            result = self._inner.unwrap_key(handle, wrapped_key, wrap_nonce)
536	        except (ValueError, TypeError, ProviderError):
537	            raise
538	        except Exception as exc:
539	            raise ProviderUnavailable(
540	                "provider %r operation unwrap_key failed" % self.provider_id
541	            ) from exc
542	        if not isinstance(result, bytes) or len(result) != _DEK_LEN:
543	            raise ProviderUnavailable(
544	                "provider returned a malformed data key from unwrap_key"
545	            )
546	        return result

548	    def health(self) -> bool:
549	        """Optional readiness probe normalized to a bool.
550	
551	        A provider without a ``health`` method is treated as ready. A method
552	        that raises, returns a non-bool, or returns ``False`` reports
553	        unavailable; any backend text is swallowed here and never reaches a
554	        client.
555	        """
556	        method = getattr(self._inner, "health", None)
557	        if method is None:
558	            # Missing health() means healthy by contract.
559	            return True
560	        try:
561	            result = method()
562	        except Exception:
563	            return False
564	        # Only the exact bool True is healthy; a bool False, a truthy
565	        # non-bool (1, "yes", ...) and any other object mean unavailable.
566	        return result is True

570	    """Whether a bound provider declares the optional ``sign`` operation.
571	
572	    Declaration is purely by ``capabilities["operations"]`` containing
573	    ``"sign"``: a declaring external provider was contract-validated to have
574	    a callable ``sign`` method, and the built-in local provider always
575	    declares and implements it. Anything else (including a provider whose
576	    capabilities are not a mapping) keeps the export-based signing path.
577	    """
578	    caps = getattr(provider, "capabilities", None)
579	    if not isinstance(caps, dict):
580	        return False
581	    operations = caps.get("operations")
582	    if not isinstance(operations, (list, tuple)):
583	        return False
584	    return OP_SIGN in operations

593	    always declares and implements it. Anything else (including a provider
594	    whose capabilities are not a mapping) keeps the export-based decrypt

598	    if not isinstance(caps, dict):

1078	# -- non-disruptive reconnect gate -----------------------------------------
1079	# Reconnect and ordinary provider calls share ONE five-second budget per
1080	# attempt, measured from its FIRST wait or health probe. The ordering the gate
1081	# enforces is:
1082	#
1083	#   1. a reconnect first establishes a cross-process *intent* (an exclusive
1084	#      flock on ``provider-reconnect.lock``), THEN drains the calls admitted
1085	#      before it;
1086	#   2. every LATER call waits -- in every process -- from the instant intent
1087	#      is visible until the candidate is built, contract-validated, health
1088	#      probed, ``provider-state.json`` is committed and the swap finished;
1089	#   3. calls admitted before the intent was established keep running on the
1090	#      OLD provider instance they captured and are simply drained.
1091	#
1092	# The extra intent file is required because a blocking exclusive flock alone
1093	# is NOT a barrier on Linux: new shared-lock requests leapfrog a queued
1094	# exclusive waiter (verified on the host kernel), so later calls would slip
1095	# past a reconnect that had only *queued* for ``provider-state.lock`` and a
1096	# steady call stream could starve it. Ordinary calls therefore never hold the
1097	# intent lock for their duration; they only probe it with an instant
1098	# non-blocking shared trylock, once before and once after taking their shared
1099	# state lease, and fall back to waiting when the probe catches a reconnect.

1101	_POLL_SECONDS = 0.02
1102	#: Per-probe cap for a health probe on the ORDINARY call path. One attempt's
1103	#: probes all draw on its single non-resettable :data:`CALL_GATE_SECONDS`
1104	#: budget as well: a probe waits at most the smaller of one second and the
1105	#: budget remainder, and a result landing only after that wait is void.
1106	HEALTH_PROBE_SECONDS = 1.0

1111	
1112	    The deadline starts lazily at the first blocking wait OR the first
1113	    bounded health probe (``start`` is idempotent), so an attempt admitted
1114	    without contention spends no budget on the gate itself; every later
1115	    wait, poll and bounded probe shares one non-resettable deadline.
1116	    """
1117	
1118	    def __init__(self, seconds: Optional[float] = None) -> None:
1119	        self.seconds = CALL_GATE_SECONDS if seconds is None else seconds
1120	        self._deadline: Optional[float] = None
1121	
1122	    def start(self) -> float:
1123	        if self._deadline is None:
1124	            self._deadline = time.monotonic() + self.seconds
1125	        return self._deadline
1126	
1127	    @property
1128	    def deadline(self) -> float:
1129	        return self.start()
1130	
1131	    def remaining(self) -> float:
1132	        return max(0.0, self.deadline - time.monotonic())
1133

1160	# -- committed cross-process provider state ---------------------------------
1161	# ``provider-state.json`` (0600) is the single cross-process record of which
1162	# provider is active in a data directory and which generation of it was last
1163	# committed. It is written atomically (temp file, fsync, rename) by the first
1164	# healthy activation, by every successful reconnect and by the two commits of
1165	# every provider switch, as compact UTF-8 JSON with the fixed key order
1166	# ``schema_version,provider_id,target_provider_id,generation,reason,phase``,

1628	    """A held shared/exclusive ``flock`` on a gate lock file.
1629	
1630	    This is the cross-process half of the reconnect gate: provider calls
1631	    hold a shared lease for their whole duration (in-flight calls in every
1632	    process finish before a reconnect commits), while a reconnect commit or
1633	    a first activation takes the exclusive lease. Acquisition polls with a
1634	    non-blocking flock against the shared five-second deadline; a wait past
1635	    it raises :class:`ProviderReconnectPending` with zero side effects. When
1636	    no data directory is bound (or fcntl is unavailable) the lease is a
1637	    no-op and the in-process gate alone applies.
1638	    """

1640	    def __init__(self, lock_name: str = _STATE_LOCK_NAME) -> None:
1641	        self._lock_name = lock_name
1642	        self._fd: Optional[int] = None
1643	
1644	    def acquire(self, exclusive: bool, deadline: float) -> None:
1645	        self.release()
1646	        if _configured_dir is None or fcntl is None:
1647	            return
1648	        try:
1649	            os.makedirs(_configured_dir, exist_ok=True)
1650	            fd = os.open(
1651	                os.path.join(_configured_dir, self._lock_name),
1652	                os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT,
1653	                0o600,
1654	            )
1655	        except OSError as exc:
1656	            raise ProviderUnavailable(
1657	                "cannot open provider state lock: %s" % exc
1658	            ) from exc
1659	        operation = fcntl.LOCK_EX if exclusive else fcntl.LOCK_SH
1660	        try:
1661	            while True:
1662	                try:
1663	                    fcntl.flock(fd, operation | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
1664	                    break
1665	                except InterruptedError:
1666	                    continue
1667	                except OSError as exc:
1668	                    if exc.errno not in (
1669	                        errno.EACCES,
1670	                        errno.EAGAIN,
1671	                        errno.EWOULDBLOCK,
1672	                    ):
1673	                        raise
1674	                    remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
1675	                    if remaining <= 0:
1676	                        raise ProviderReconnectPending(
1677	                            "timed out waiting for the cross-process "
1678	                            "provider gate"
1679	                        )

"""KMS/HSM provider abstraction.

Every private key is owned by a *provider*: a local software key store by
default, or an external KMS/HSM reached through the ``module:factory`` entry
point named by ``KEYMGR_PROVIDER``. The rest of the package never touches raw
key material when a provider is in use: it only persists the opaque
``provider_id`` / ``handle`` / ``encrypted_material`` triple a provider
returns, and asks the provider to turn a handle back into exportable material.

Primary/standby failover
------------------------
``KEYMGR_PROVIDER_CHAIN`` may name a comma-separated list of ``local`` /
``module:factory`` entries (entries and their built ``provider_id`` values
must be unique; an unset variable falls back to ``KEYMGR_PROVIDER``, while a
set-but-empty, empty-item or malformed chain is unusable). The first healthy
entry is activated. Every ORDINARY provider call then shares ONE
non-resettable five-second budget started at its first wait or probe: every
gate wait and every health probe of the attempt draws on the same deadline,
and a single ``health()`` probe is additionally capped at one second. A probe
returning exactly ``True`` clears the persisted failure count and proceeds;
``False``, a non-bool, a raised probe, one past its wait, or a result that
arrives only after the wait (void -- it never counts as anything but the
timeout) increments the active entry's persisted failure count (capped at
three) and pins the call to the fixed 503. The first two failures never
switch; after the third failure the call uses the REMAINDER of the same
five-second budget to re-verify the active entry (still at most one second
per probe) -- recovery clears the count and serves the call -- and otherwise
probes the standby entries in chain order under the same cross-process
intent/drain gate a reconnect uses, failing over exactly once to the first
healthy standby (a single ``switching`` then ``ready`` commit, generation
plus one) and continuing in the new generation. Old calls finish on the
instance they captured, later calls land on the new generation, and
concurrent third strikes build/commit exactly once. With no healthy standby
(or on a gate timeout) the old generation is retained. The threshold lives in
``provider-health.json`` (a 0600 satellite of a READY ``provider-state.json``
with the same id and generation), so it survives restarts and is shared
across processes; a corrupt, ahead or same-generation-wrong-id health record
is a fixed 503 that is never rewritten. A recovered primary is never
re-selected automatically; only ``reconnect`` re-selects the first healthy
entry, while ``switchover`` moves the active provider to one NAMED chain
entry under the same gate (``switching`` then ``ready`` commits, reason
``reconnect``). Pending idempotent operations stay bound to their original
``provider_id`` and are never replayed on a standby.

Provider contract
-----------------
A provider instance exposes:

* ``provider_id``: a non-empty string;
* ``capabilities``: ``{"algorithms": ["AES256", "RSA2048"],
  "operations": ["generate", "rotate", "import_material",
  "export_material", "delete"]}``;
* ``generate(algorithm)`` / ``rotate(algorithm)`` ->
  ``{"handle", "public_key", "encrypted_material"}``;
* ``import_material(algorithm, public_key, material)`` -> the same triple;
* ``export_material(handle)`` -> ``{"public_key", "encrypted_material"}``;
* ``delete(handle)`` -> ``None``, idempotent;
* ``health()`` -> ``bool``, *optional*. A missing method is treated as ready;
  a method that raises or returns anything but a real bool reports unavailable.
  The probe's own text never leaves the process.

Native signing (optional)
-------------------------
``capabilities["operations"]`` MAY additionally list ``"sign"``. Declaring it
makes ``sign(handle: str, message: bytes) -> bytes`` contractual: a provider
that declares the operation without a callable ``sign`` method fails the
contract (and a declared-but-non-callable ``sign`` attribute is invalid too).
The method signs with RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5/SHA-256 inside the KMS/HSM and returns
the 256-byte signature; private material never crosses the boundary. A handle
that is not a non-empty string raises ``ValueError``, a non-bytes message
raises ``TypeError``, and an unknown handle, a handle that is not an RSA key,
or any backend failure raises :class:`ProviderUnavailable`. When a version's
owning provider declares ``sign``, the service calls it on the bound provider
inside the ordinary five-second provider-call gate, never calls
``export_material`` for signing and never loads the private key into the
service process; it verifies the returned signature against the version's
stored public key and treats a malformed result, a failed verification or any
provider exception as the fixed 503 (no audit event). A provider that does
NOT declare ``sign`` keeps the export-based signing path. The built-in local
provider declares and implements ``sign``.

Native DEK unwrap (optional)
----------------------------
``capabilities["operations"]`` MAY additionally list ``"unwrap_key"``.
Declaring it makes
``unwrap_key(handle: str, wrapped_key: bytes, wrap_nonce: bytes | None = None) -> bytes``
contractual: a provider that declares the operation without a callable
``unwrap_key`` method fails the contract (and a declared-but-non-callable
``unwrap_key`` attribute is invalid too). The method unwraps a
``keymgr-envelope-v1`` data key inside the KMS/HSM and returns the 32-byte
DEK; the KEK's private material never crosses the boundary. A handle that is
not a non-empty string raises ``ValueError``; a non-bytes ``wrapped_key`` or
a non-null non-bytes ``wrap_nonce`` raises ``TypeError``; an empty
``wrapped_key``, an AES256 ``wrap_nonce`` that is not exactly 12 bytes or an
RSA2048 ``wrap_nonce`` that is not null raises ``ValueError``; an unknown
handle, a handle whose algorithm does not fit the request, or any backend
failure raises :class:`ProviderUnavailable`; an authentication failure (a
tampered or wrong-key ``wrapped_key``) raises
:class:`ProviderInvalidMaterial`. When a version's owning provider declares
``unwrap_key``, the service's decrypt path calls it on the bound provider
inside the ordinary five-second provider-call gate, never calls
``export_material`` and never loads the KEK private key into the service
process; an authentication failure surfaces as a 400 naming the envelope,
while a malformed result or any provider fault is the fixed 503 (no audit
event). A provider that does NOT declare ``unwrap_key`` keeps the
export-based decrypt path. The built-in local provider declares and
implements ``unwrap_key``.

The factory named by ``KEYMGR_PROVIDER=module:factory`` is imported lazily on
first use and called with no arguments. A missing module/factory, a factory
raising, or a returned object failing the contract all raise
:class:`ProviderUnavailable`; the service answers ``503`` (CLI exit ``1``) and
never falls back to the local provider.
"""
